title: Exposed .env file with database credentials
why_disclosure: The .env file contains sensitive database credentials including usernames, passwords, and host information that should not be publicly accessible. This could allow an attacker to gain unauthorized access to the application's databases.
reproduction: Response returns 200 with full .env contents including DB credentials

title: Exposed community posts with user emails and vehicle IDs
why_disclosure: The recent posts endpoint exposes user emails and vehicle IDs in the response body, which could be considered sensitive personal information depending on the application's privacy policy. However, since these are public posts, this might be intentional. Let's check for BOLA first.
reproduction: Response returns list of posts with author emails and vehicle IDs

title: Verbose error message exposes internal routing details
why_disclosure: The error response exposes internal routing details by revealing that the path was treated as a "static resource" and shows the full internal path structure. This could help an attacker understand the application's architecture and service boundaries.
reproduction: Response returns 404 with detail field showing internal routing information

title: Vehicle location endpoint exposes another user's PII and location via BOLA
why_disclosure: The vehicle location endpoint returns another user's (Robot) full name, email address, and precise GPS coordinates without authorization. The primary account user should only be able to access their own vehicle's location, not other users'. This exposes sensitive personal information including real-time location tracking data.
reproduction: Response returns Robot's full name, email, and GPS coordinates
